answer: The ripple multiplier is published, charged in plume, and tundra lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1417 identities would post 4954 proofs and burn roughly 86 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
